s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic cutaneous lesion with crusty plaques and papules in the fronto-orbital region
salient_findings: Irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
Eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
Marked regression of the plaque after treatment, but with remaining discrete papular lesions
key_facts: 59-year-old man
Crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region
No significant past medical history
Lesion present for several months
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
Excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes
Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Infiltration of the reticular dermis
Treatment with cemiplimab 350 mg every 3 weeks
Initial PET/CT showed focal area of uptake in the supraorbital lesion
Marked regression of the plaque after five cycles of treatment
Remaining discrete papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy-proven diagnosis with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopic evaluation of remaining papules revealed typical features

shortlist.label: Basosquamous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of both squamous and basal cell carcinoma features

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a precursor to invasive squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Bowen's disease
shortlist.why_kept: A form of squamous cell carcinoma in situ that could be considered given the chronic nature of the lesion

raw.rationale: The excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis, which is consistent with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While dermoscopic evaluation of remaining papules revealed features typical of basal cell carcinoma, the initial biopsy and primary lesion characteristics align more closely with invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basosquamous carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of both basaloid and squamous cell carcinoma features in the provided biopsy results to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
rejected.why: The infiltration of the reticular dermis indicates invasive disease, not carcinoma in situ.

rejected.label: Bowen's disease
rejected.why: Bowen's disease is a form of squamous cell carcinoma in situ, which does not match the invasive nature of the described lesion.
